research_question: What is the effect of selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs), administered either continuously or in the luteal phase, compared with placebo, on self-rated overall premenstrual symptom severity at the end of treatment in women with PMS or PMDD?
outcome_description: Self-rated overall (total) premenstrual symptom severity score measured on validated scales at the end of treatment
positive_direction: Greater reduction in overall self-rated premenstrual symptoms favoring SSRI over placebo
search_queries: SSRI premenstrual dysphoric disorder randomized controlled trial
selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor premenstrual syndrome trial outcome
fluoxetine sertraline premenstrual symptoms placebo comparison
inclusion_criteria: Women diagnosed with premenstrual syndrome (PMS) or premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD)
Randomized or controlled clinical trials comparing an SSRI (continuous or luteal-phase dosing) to placebo
Quantitative assessment of post-treatment self-rated overall premenstrual symptom severity on a validated instrument
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, editorials, opinion pieces, and theoretical papers are excluded)
No comparison between an SSRI treatment arm and a placebo control condition
No quantitative outcome data that can produce an effect size for self-rated overall premenstrual symptom severity (means and SDs, change scores, or test statistics required)
Studies evaluating only non-SSRI pharmacotherapies or reporting exclusively clinician-rated scales, single isolated symptoms, functioning, or adverse events without overall symptom totals
moderators_to_extract: Specific SSRI agent (e.g., fluoxetine, sertraline, paroxetine, escitalopram, citalopram)
Outcome measurement instrument (e.g., Daily Record of Severity of Problems [DRSP], Daily Symptom Report [DSR], Visual Analogue Scale [VAS])
Treatment duration (number of cycles or weeks)
effect_size_note: When trials include multiple SSRI arms versus a single placebo group, divide the placebo sample size equally across comparisons to avoid unit-of-analysis error. Continuous end-of-treatment scores on validated self-report scales are extracted.
